title: Ingest sidecar slow-path health forwarder and replay shim
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Add a lightweight sidecar component and health-forwarding shim to surface slow-path ingestion (schema negotiation failures, enriched-event requeues, backpressure-affected flows) into our observability pipeline. The sidecar will emit compact health envelopes and a replayable pointer to original payloads for controlled re-ingestion. This reduces blindspots when structured log adapters fall back to slow-path processing and enables end-to-end correlation for tenant troubleshooting.
background: We've observed intermittent spikes where the structured ingest adapters (JSON/Protobuf) fall back to a slow-path: reparse attempts, schema negotiation, and small-batch reingestion. These events currently generate sparse logs and missing correlation anchors in Loki/ELK, making incident triage slow. Existing ingest proxies provide metrics but not a lightweight, consistent envelope that ties directly to original request IDs and replay handles.
technical_design: Sidecar runs adjacent to ingress proxy as a small Rust binary (low overhead) that listens on a unix socket for health events and replay requests.
Health envelope schema: {timestamp, tenant_id, ingest_path, event_type, corr_id, original_request_ptr (storage key), reason_code, sample_rate, kv_meta} — stored as compact JSON with fixed fields.
Forwarding: sidecar forwards envelopes to a dedicated Loki tenant stream and to an ELK input (via kafka topic) with a high-priority routing header.

Replay shim: when slow-path events are flagged, sidecar writes a pointer to blob store (S3) and emits envelope with original_request_ptr. A controller can re-ingest using that pointer and tag replay-run ids for observability.
Backpressure handling: sidecar exposes token-bucket and drops non-sampled envelopes when saturated; emits dropped-envelope metrics to alerting.

Correlation: sidecar attaches standard corr_id and falls back to generated session_fingerprint when missing. Corr_id will be cross-referenced with tracing hooks via OTEL span id mapping stored in a compact index service.
Security: pointers to original payloads are stored encrypted (KMS) and TTL-limited. Access controlled by service principal; UI and support playbooks will surface one-time replay links.
Compatibility: ingest proxies will send a single-line JSON health event to the sidecar; adapters that cannot connect will emit to a dead-letter kafka with the same envelope schema for later pickup.
Operational controls: feature flag gated per-tenant; sample rate configurable through Console; retention policy and high-cost tenant opt-out supported.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar binary deployed to staging ingest nodes; accepts health envelope over unix socket and verifies schema validity.
Sidecar forwards envelopes to Loki stream with correct tenant header and preserves corr_id in labels.
Replay pointers stored in S3 encrypted with KMS and can be used by a reingest controller to replay payload in staging.
Metrics emitted: health_envelope_count, health_envelope_dropped, replay_requested, replay_success, replay_failure. Dashboards added to Console with per-tenant breakdown.
Canary rollout plan executed with 5% of tenants on staging and 1% in prod, no elevated error budget burn observed.
Security review completed for pointer storage and access controls.
migration_plan: 1) Roll out sidecar to ingest-staging nodes and collect envelopes for two weeks.
2) Run reconciliation to ensure sidecar and current telemetry correlate > 95% for slow-path events.
3) Enable replay for a small set of non-critical tenants and validate end-to-end ingestion fidelity.
4) Gradually enable feature flag for production tenants in cohorts, monitor costs and dropped envelope rates.
5) Deprecate ad-hoc error logs and consolidate observability to the health envelope stream.
6) Document playbooks and grant support team single-click replay access with audit trails.
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of edge nodes, 48 hour observation window.
Stage: 20% of tenants, enable replay for 3 non-critical tenants.
Prod ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 3 weeks contingent on SLOs.
Kill-switch: Console flag to disable forwarding per-region and per-tenant.
Communication: post-mortem and runbook updates to oncall channel + infra-announce.
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope schema validation and KMS encryption wrappers.
Integration test that writes pointer to S3 and verifies reingest controller consumes it.
Chaos test: drop sidecar connectivity and ensure ingest proxy falls back to dead-letter with identical envelope.
Load test: simulate 10k health events/minute and verify sidecar CPU < 5% of node baseline and Loki stream handles throughput.
E2E canary with synthetic slow-path traces to verify Console dashboards surface incidents and links to replay blobs.

2026-03-07: Security (Rina Shah) - Confirmed KMS flow is acceptable; requested threat model doc and short retention justification.
2026-03-09: Eng review (Infra) - Raised concern about Loki label cardinality; agreed to attach a small set of normalized labels and push JSON body to blobstore only.
